generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential 1..N per table, NOT NULL, no reuse
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from parent PK pool; allow parent-without-child rows by skipping some parent PKs in child tables; NULL where nullable
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Pick from a small curated pool per column; allow case variants and near-duplicates for columns with LIKE/equality boundaries
generic_sampling_rules.numeric_amount: Integer; sample from a uniform range centered on observed median; allow ties at ORDER ranks
generic_sampling_rules.numeric_real: REAL with one decimal place; sample in observed range
generic_sampling_rules.flag_enum: Small integer set IN (0,1) where applicable
generic_sampling_rules.null_share_default: 0.0 for NOT NULL and PK columns; for nullable columns insert NULL in at least 1 row per instance
generic_sampling_rules.distinct_duplicates: On DISTINCT columns, ensure duplicate share 20-50% by repeating values
generic_sampling_rules.tie_at_limit: Ensure at least two rows tie at rank 1 for ORDER DESC columns

issues.evidence: Specification lists 'Campuses.County' comparison_boundary targets as literals ['Orange'] plus values [199,200,201], and the atomic-op extraction shows PRED(campuses.county > 200) alongside county='Orange'. County is TEXT; the numeric 199/200/201 boundary is a type-mismatched artifact of literal routing (the same 199/200/201 pool is shared with enrollments FTE/TotalEnrollment). spec.py NUM_BOUNDARY['Campuses.County']=[199,200,201] and _init_sampler casts these into a StringSampler boundary, so '199','200','201' strings get planted into County. This is harmless (no integrity violation, no formula) but semantically odd.
issues.requested_revision: Optional: drop the numeric 199/200/201 pool from Campuses.County in the spec (keep only 'Orange'/'orange' case variants), since County is TEXT and the numeric boundary belongs to enrollments. Not blocking.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: 'Campuses.Campus: generated rows: NULL 0 / 58', 'Campuses.County: NULL 0 / 58', 'Campuses.Location: NULL 0 / 58', 'Campuses.Year: NULL 0 / 58'. These columns are not in spec.NULL_TARGETS, so _apply_null_rule skips them; the compact DB apparently has 0 NULL share for them, so 0 NULLs is consistent with the interface rule (share follows compact share, at least one NULL only for nullable columns with nonzero share). No violation, but noted per instruction 7.
issues.requested_revision: None required; noted for the engineer that these columns produce no NULLs because their compact share is 0 and they are not in NULL_TARGETS.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_ties plants ties only for degrees.Degrees and csu_fees.CampusFee. The spec also lists ties_for_order_limit for degrees.Year (on SUM/AVG(degrees.degrees)) and degrees.Campus (on AVG/SUM(degrees.degrees)). These are aggregate-level ties, not single-column ties; _plant_group_sizes does force repeated degrees.Year values (GROUP_SIZE_PLAN), which can produce aggregate ties, but there is no explicit guarantee. construction_pairs separated=20/52 with no per-group breakdown, so tie separation for these aggregate patterns is unverified.
issues.requested_revision: Optional: add an explicit check/plant that at least two degrees.Year groups (and two degrees.Campus groups) tie at rank 1 on SUM/AVG(degrees.degrees), or document that group-size planting is relied upon. Not blocking since the program runs cleanly and integrity holds.

reviews.summary: Program runs reproducibly (20/20 valid, 0 FK/NOT NULL/PK violations, 0 failures), preserves compact rows (copy + append), and implements the specified table sizes, year/numeric boundary pools, LIKE/case variants, NULL rule (share-based, at least one NULL for nullable targets), non-negativity and FTE_AY<=TotalEnrollment_AY formulas, and FK dependencies. Semantic rules are supported by the compact data (FTE<=Total, year boundaries). Minor spec oddity (numeric pool on TEXT County) and unverified aggregate-tie patterns are noted but do not block a pass.
